messages.subject: multilevel multi-logit regression error
parts:
I'm trying to perform point estimation with a hierarchical multi-logit regression model.  I've tried to combine the multi-logit regression model and the hierarchical logistic regression model examples in the manual.  This is the error I get:

Initialization between (-2, 2) failed after 100 attempts. 
 Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model.


Here is the model file:

data {
    int<lower=2> numOutcome;
    int<lower=0> numData;
    int<lower=1> numPredictor;
    int<lower=1> numPeople;
    int<lower=1,upper=numOutcome> y[numData];
    vector[numPredictor] x[numData];
    int<lower=1,upper=numPeople> label[numData];
}

parameters {
    matrix[numOutcome,numPredictor] beta[numPeople];
}

model {
    for (l in 1:numPeople)
        for (k in 1:numOutcome)
            beta[l][k] ~ normal(0,5);
    for (n in 1:numData)
        y[n] ~ categorical(softmax(beta[label[n]] * x[n]));
}

Here is the input preparation file.  BTW, I'm using a small random sample from the original, large dataset "allData" to test things out.

numOutcome = length(unique(allData[,1]))
numData=1000
numPredictor = ncol(allData) - 2
randomIndices <- sample(1:length(V1), numData, replace=FALSE)
sampleFrame = allData[randomIndices,]
numPeople = max(unique(sampleFrame[,2]))
y = sampleFrame[,1]
x = sampleFrame[,3:4]
labels = sampleFrame[,2]

myData = list(numOutcome=numOutcome, numData=numData, numPredictor=numPredictor,
              numPeople=numPeople, x=x, y=y, label=labels)

m = stan_model(file='model_2.stan')
f = optimizing(m,data=myData)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multilevel multi-logit regression error
parts:
In general, you can use print statements to debug where things
go wrong. I don't see how the normal could fail, but you
could underflow or overflow and run into problems with softmax.

Could you try init=0 and see if that works? It will initialize
the matrix of coefficients to 0 and should prevent initial overflow.

Also, it's more stable to write this:

y[n] ~ categorical_logit(beta[label[n]] * x[n]);

We can save a round trip exp and log in the middle that helps
prevent some overflow/underflow.

I don't see anywhere your program could get tripped up by
indexing.

- Bob
